text:
maria: Quick question — ruby sampleapp calls to Redwood are failing for OIDC-authenticated flows. upstream returns 400.
elaine: Any stack traces or request dumps?
maria: gist of the log: 
```
Net::HTTPBadResponse: wrong status line: "GET /v1/..."
```
sam: That usually means the request was mangled. Can you dump the raw HTTP?
maria: Captured raw request header. Authorization header ends mid-JWT (token is ~3.2k chars). Looks truncated.
ryan: Where is the sampleapp running? Could be proxy chopping long headers.
maria: Local docker-compose with our small ingress (envoy-lite) in front of the app. If I bypass the proxy and hit the backend directly, the token is intact and requests succeed.
elaine: Envoy default header limits are pretty big. Another possibility is the app helper adding a newline or control char into the header value.
sam: Good call. Could you grep the auth helper for any "\n" or "\r" being appended when building the header?
maria: Found it: the auth connector did `headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{token}\n"`. Removing the trailing newline makes the request happy through the proxy.
ryan: Newline in a header value can make the proxy parse it as a folded header and drop the remainder. Classic.
elaine: Let's patch the sampleapp helper to sanitize tokens: `token.strip` or `token.gsub(/[\r\n]/, '')` before setting header.
sam: I suggest adding a tiny unit test that simulates constructing headers and asserts there are no control characters in values. Also mirror behavior from Go sample: it trims whitespace when setting Authorization.
ryan: I'll open a small PR: trim token, add unit, include a short note in troubleshooting docs about proxies and long JWTs.
maria: Thanks! I'll test the change against our enterprise ingress tomorrow.
devops-bot: CI build queued: https://ci.redwood/sampleapp/7890 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
devops-bot: CI passed: https://ci.redwood/sampleapp/7890 :white_check_mark:
elaine: Also add a line in Quickstart: "If auth headers appear truncated, check for stray newlines/control chars in SDK helpers and verify ingress header size/limits."
sam: +1. That will save a lot of puzzling debugging in user support.
maria: Patch LGTM locally. Will watch the enterprise proxy test. :thumbsup:
